0AAF54.confound_note: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, so a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before and that every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell, so the extra water reached every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, so the rain and the drip line moved together and the 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be attributed to the line. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.

Doubled rainfall falling directly on all four open-ground maize blocks explains the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gain over the previous summer as well as the drip line does.

Rainfall is a live alternative cause that reaches every unit: "Rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before, and every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell." 49435F.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and the clause beside it records that about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile. The claim is about board defects on the run, so the population is every board built on it and the defect figures describe nine tenths of that. Boards that take a pass on the old profile are the ones routed off the normal flow, and the extra handling and the extra heat cycle raise a board's defect risk on their own, so a rate built on the untouched boards alone sits below the run's own rate and the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent are consistent with defect production holding flat. The four runs sit on the Aspen, Kestrel, Larkspur and Meridian lines across four different months, and the same tenth falls outside the tally on each, so the spread over lines, board families and months does nothing to close the gap.
descriptions: The defect rates are computed on a filtered subset: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." Roughly a tenth of each run is excluded from the new-profile figure while the prior-month baseline is the whole line, so the 4-7 percent drop compares a narrower, self-selected population against a broader one.

The defect rates "cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout" while "about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile" - that tenth is excluded from the new-profile numbers but was included in the earlier-period baseline, and boards diverted to an old-profile pass are the likeliest to be defective, so the 4-7 percent improvement is partly an artefact of dropping them.
match_notes: Baseline-vs-after framing is an elaboration of the same excluded tenth, not a second defect.

ED27C1.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the timings over the runs that stayed on the issued route, and the clause beside it records that about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route. The claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, so the population is every run dispatched and the minute figures describe roughly five sixths of it. A run leaves the issued route when it meets a blockage or a diversion, which is exactly what makes a run come in long, so an average taken over the runs that stayed on it sits below the figure for all runs dispatched, and the reductions of 8, 5, 9 and 6 minutes are consistent with no reduction at all. Every case is vans out of Kettleby Wharf in February under dispatcher Verhoeven, so one and the same exclusion sits under all four groups at once.
descriptions: The outcome is measured on a self-selected subset: "Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route." The measured population is narrower than the claim: 'Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route', while 'about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route' and are therefore excluded. The runs most likely to abandon a new route are the ones where it went badly, so the 5-9 minute saving is computed on a filtered subset rather than on the routing change's actual effect.
match_notes: Names the excluded sixth that left the issued route and why it biases the average.

A9D2D3.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed. "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - the 6-11 point gains omit the fifth of trays sown from partly coated seed, so the figures cover a selected subset of each lot rather than the lots the coating was applied to.
